text:
The traveler who crossed Les Halles as summer fell

walked on tiptoe

Despair made its great yarrow plants whirl in the sky, so beautiful

And in the handbag lay my dream, that vial of salts

which only God's godmother inhaled

The torpors unfolded like vapor

in the Smoking Dog

where pro and con had just entered

The girl could be seen by them only poorly and askance

I had to deal with the ambassador of saltpeter

or with the white curve on a black background we call thought

The dance of the innocents was at its height

The little lanterns slowly lit among the chestnut trees

The lady without a shadow knelt on the Pont au Change

On Gît-le-Coeur Street the bells were no longer the same

The promises of the nights were finally being fulfilled

The carrier pigeons, the kisses of rescue

joined themselves to the breasts of the beautiful unknown

thrown beneath the crêpe of perfect meanings

A farm flourished in the middle of Paris

and its windows looked out over the Milky Way

But no one inhabited it yet because of the apparitions

of the apparitions who, as everyone knows, are more devout

than the disappeared

Some, like this woman, seem to swim

and a little of their substance enters love

She internalizes them

I am no toy of any sensory power

And yet the cricket that sang in the ash-colored hair

one afternoon near the statue of Étienne Marcel

winked at me in understanding

André Breton told me, come in

translation.title: Sunflower
translation.editorial_note: Les Halles, Pont au Change, Gît-le-Coeur, and Étienne Marcel are retained as Parisian referents; “yaros” is rendered as yarrow.
